answer:
Your records come from six places (Kestrel Harbor Hospital, Fernhill Family Clinic, Saltmarsh ED, Northbay Labs, Clearwater Eye and Alder Street Pharmacy), and they stop in mid-July 2026. Anything done since then, or done somewhere that isn't in them, won't show up here. Here is what I would raise, most important first.

1. A lung nodule that was never followed up (most urgent). The CT you had in the Saltmarsh ER on Oct 18, 2025 for the kidney stone also picked up a 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a non-contrast chest CT in 6-12 months, so the window ran from April to Oct 18, 2026 and has now closed. I find no chest CT and no mention of the nodule anywhere else. Most nodules like this are harmless, and you have never smoked, which lowers the risk. It still needs that scan, so ask for it now.

2. Hydrochlorothiazide: the records disagree about whether you should be taking it. You were admitted to Kestrel Harbor on March 2, 2026 with dizziness, a fall and a sodium of 123. The hospital blamed hydrochlorothiazide and told you to stop it on March 5. But Alder Street Pharmacy filled it on April 2 (90 days, 2 refills left, still marked active), you told the eye clinic on May 14 that you take it, and Fernhill's June 2026 list still shows it as active. Your sodium was low again (134) on June 15. The pharmacy did not refill it on June 28 the way it did your other pills, so you may have stopped. The records can't tell me. Please tell Dr. Marsh exactly what you are taking, and don't start or stop anything on the strength of this note alone.

3. A thyroid recheck that was asked for and not done. Your TSH was mildly high (7.9) during the March stay, with a normal free T4. The discharge instructions asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated in 6-8 weeks, which would have been around late April. I see no repeat.

4. Fernhill doesn't seem to know about your outside care. Dr. Marsh's problem list (June 2026) shows hay fever, high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. It doesn't show the kidney stone, the lung nodule or the March hospital stay. The ER asked you to see your primary care doctor within a week, and the hospital asked for a visit within 1-2 weeks. I find no visit or note about either. Nothing records whether the stone passed or whether you saw urology. It's worth bringing the discharge papers.

5. Cholesterol. Your LDL was 142 and HDL 48 in Sept 2025, and it has not been rechecked. You have diabetes, and you are 57. Guidelines generally advise a statin for people aged 40-75 with diabetes. No statin appears on any of your medication lists and no discussion of one is recorded. Ask whether one is right for you.

6. Diabetes checks that aren't in the records. Your A1c is improving (6.9, then 6.7, then 6.6) and your June 2026 kidney function was normal. But I find no urine albumin-to-creatinine test, which is recommended yearly for people with diabetes, and no foot exam. You were referred to diabetes education in Sept 2025, but nothing shows you went. (The ER urine dipstick showed no protein, but that isn't the same test.)

7. Vaccines. On Nov 8, 2025 the pharmacy gave you flu, Prevnar 20 and the first Shingrix. The second Shingrix dose is normally due 2-6 months after the first, and none is recorded. No flu shot is recorded since November 2025, so this season's dose may be due. I also find no record of tetanus (Td/Tdap), COVID or hepatitis B vaccines, which are commonly advised for adults with diabetes. These may simply have been given somewhere else.

8. Women's cancer screening. I see no mammogram and no cervical screening (Pap or HPV test) anywhere. These are often done at outside centers, so they may exist. If you can't find them, ask about getting them, since you turn 58 on Nov 4.

9. Allergy lists don't match. Fernhill lists lisinopril (dry cough) as an intolerance, but the hospital, ER, pharmacy and eye clinic lists show only aspirin. The hospital's own medication list says lisinopril was stopped for cough. Also, your aspirin reaction was recorded as mild in April 2025 and as moderate from May 2025 on. Ask each place to update its list.

10. Things that look on track. Your colonoscopy on April 16, 2019 was normal, with a repeat advised in 10 years (2029). Your dilated eye exam on May 14, 2026 showed no diabetic retinopathy, and the eye clinic wants you back in 12 months. Your blood pressure on June 15, 2026 was 128/80, which Dr. Marsh called at goal.

This is a review of your paperwork, not a diagnosis. Dr. Marsh can sort out what applies to you.
short: Please review: (1) 7 mm right-lower-lobe lung nodule found on the Oct 18, 2025 ER CT; the 6-12 month chest CT is not on record and is now past due. (2) Hydrochlorothiazide was stopped on Mar 5, 2026 for hyponatremia, but it was refilled on Apr 2 and is still listed as active, and sodium was 134 on Jun 15. (3) The repeat TSH/free T4 (TSH 7.9 in March) was not done. Also not in my records: statin or lipid recheck, urine albumin, Shingrix dose 2, mammogram and cervical screening.

knowledge.says: For a single solid nodule of 6-8 mm in a low-risk person, a repeat CT at 6-12 months is advised, with a further CT at 18-24 months considered. Most such nodules are benign, but follow-up is how the rare cancer is caught early.
knowledge.guideline: Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines for incidental pulmonary nodules

knowledge.says: ACE-inhibitor cough is a drug intolerance rather than a true allergy, but it should be recorded so the drug isn't restarted. Switching to a drug of the ARB class, like losartan, is the usual fix. Hives from aspirin can also mean other NSAIDs like ibuprofen aren't safe, which is why the ER avoided them.
